headline: Child kidnapping caught on CCTV in Dhaka, still missing after two days
summary: A 7-year-old child was abducted from Sheorapara, Dhaka, on Thursday afternoon. CCTV footage shows a young woman leading the child away, but the child remains missing after two days.
details: A seven-year-old child was abducted from the Sheorapara area of Kafrul Police Station in Dhaka on Thursday afternoon. Police confirmed that the kidnapping was captured on CCTV footage, but the child has not been rescued as of Friday night.
The child lived with their parents in East Sheorapara; the father works as a CNG auto-rickshaw driver. The child was playing near their home around 4:30 PM on Thursday when they disappeared.

CCTV footage from an alley next to Health Lab Diagnostic Center in East Sheorapara shows a young woman, aged 20-22, taking the child. Police suspect the woman was known to the child, as she was seen holding the child's hand.
The woman and child were then seen getting into a rickshaw. Police have traced the rickshaw's route through continuous CCTV analysis up to Agargaon, but their subsequent location remains unknown.

Kafrul Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Saiful Islam stated that the suspect, wearing a black salwar-kameez, has been identified from the footage. Police have searched nearby areas, including BNP Bosti, but the woman was not recognized there.

Beyond CCTV footage analysis, police teams are conducting raids and searching numerous rickshaw garages in hopes of finding the rickshaw, which could lead to the child. However, the rickshaw has not yet been located.
The motive for the abduction is unclear, as no ransom demand has been made even after two days. The child's relatives filed a General Diary (GD) at Kafrul Police Station on Friday.

According to a police headquarters press release, 474 children aged 1-9 were reported missing between January and July this year, with 68 still untraced. For children aged 10-17, 15,243 went missing in the same period, with 1,970 still untraced.
In total, 2,038 children from 15,717 missing reports remain untraced during this period. In 2023, 17,808 GDs were filed for missing children, followed by 16,414 in 2024 and 22,550 in 2025.

headline: 16 migrants, including 8 Bangladeshis, arrested attempting illegal entry into Indonesia from Malaysia
summary: Indonesian naval units intercepted a two-engine speedboat carrying 16 migrant workers, including eight Bangladeshis, as they attempted to enter Riau province illegally from Malaysia.
details: Sixteen migrant workers, including eight Bangladeshi nationals, were arrested by Indonesian naval units on Monday as they attempted to enter Indonesia's Riau province illegally from Malaysia. The group was intercepted while using a two-engine speedboat to cross the border.
The arrests occurred as the speedboat reached the Pantai Purnama coast in the Purnama area of West Dumai district, Dumai city. Naval forces had been monitoring the area based on intelligence reports.

Colonel Agung N Kusumazhi, head of the Dumai Naval Base, stated that intelligence was received on Sunday evening regarding the group's plan to enter the country via an illegal pier on the Pantai Mutiara coast. This information prompted the operation.

Following the intelligence, a joint team was instructed to block, monitor, and search the waters and coast of Pantai Purnama. The operation was led by Captain Wahyu Widi Bidayat, head of the naval base's intelligence unit.

Members of the operation were divided into three teams, involving the naval base's Quick Response Team and several other naval units. These included the Intelmar sea intelligence unit from Regional Naval Command I (Kodaeral-1/Belawan) and the Intelmar Operations Taskforce from Fleet Command I (Koarmada-1).
Naval teams departed from the Sungai Dumai Maritime Potential Post to participate in the operation. The successful interception highlights ongoing efforts to combat illegal migration in the region.
